notesStmt.note: These lines bear only slight resemblance to the final published poem, suggesting that they constitute an early draft, likely written in the early 1880s.

These appear to be early draft lines of the poem that was eventually published as "Last of Ebb, and Daylight Waning," appearing in the "Fancies at Navesink" cluster of November Boughs (1888). The phrase "On to oblivion" appears both in this manuscript and in the poem. The "Fancies at Navesink" cluster was first published in The Nineteenth Century magazine in August 1885.

The verso contains struck-through poetic lines that are seemingly unrelated to the lines on the recto and appear, based on the handwriting, to have been written much earlier. Their connection to Whitman's published work is unknown.

lg.head: You ebbing whirling stream's wild currents
lg.l: W You ebbing —whirling stream's wild currents

To the waning day light of life and the tide
outrunning fast,

What ardent dreams ye quench
O currents

The silent comp blasted ideals ventures
ambitions, aspirations, ‸blasted ideals, ‸burnt⹀out loves,

On—on to oblivion! On, on,
swifter deeper yet ye blessed waters ‸resperperating waters!
blessed deadly, swelling, ‸blotting, plunging, shrouding, covering waters!)
